title: Xbox CSO Issues Response To Report About GTA 6 Sales Being 'Heavily Skewed' Towards PS5
summary: "The title is breaking records for XBOX"
text: Xbox CSO Issues Response To Report About GTA 6 Sales Being 'Heavily Skewed' Towards PS5 | Pure Xbox Menu Search Share Guest Guest Login | Sign Up Pure Xbox News Reviews Features Games Guides Videos Forums Search Keywords Guest Login or Sign Up Home Choose Topics... Manage Topics News Xbox GTA 6 Xbox Series X Xbox Series S Xbox CSO Issues Response To Report About GTA 6 Sales Being 'Heavily Skewed' Towards PS5 "The title is breaking records for XBOX" by Fraser Gilbert 11 hours ago Share: Earlier this evening, the folks over at The Verge published a report that suggested GTA 6 pre-order sales were being "heavily skewed" towards PS5, and that it was "ringing yet more alarm bells about the platform" amongst other challenges that the brand has suffered recently (such as the layoffs that took place earlier this week ). This ended up getting the attention of Xbox CSO Matthew Ball, and he's taken to social media to insist that Xbox is "very happy" with GTA 6 sales so far, and that it's breaking records for the brand in the process. Here's what Ball had to say in response to The Verge's Tom Warren on social media: Tom, we are very happy with GTA VI pre-orders. The title is breaking records for XBOX, we expect even more records will be broken throughout the fall, and our internal analysis shows our share of pre-orders to be matching our share of the console market. - Matthew Ball (@ballmatthew) September 24, 2026 Ball also replied to a couple of other tweets with the words "false" and "not true" when they suggested that Xbox employees were concerned about the sales (which seemingly wasn't part of The Verge's original report anyway). You can see an example of this below: False. https://t.co/eOoAo9Rjmy - Matthew Ball (@ballmatthew) September 24, 2026 Now, of course, the mention about GTA 6 sales being "heavily skewed" towards PS5 hasn't necessarily been denied here - Ball is just keen to make clear that there's no disappointment on Xbox's side about the pre-order sales so far. It actually makes sense that the game would sell better on PlayStation than Xbox considering the difference in console sales over the past however many years, so ultimately it's not a surprise that GTA 6 will likely sell more copies on Sony's platform than Microsoft's. Nevertheless, it's evidently "breaking records" on Xbox regardless. Xbox's CSO has been very active and transparent on social media ever since taking the job earlier in 2026, and this is yet another example of that. For what it's worth, we're not insinuating this is inaccurate reporting from The Verge — they're usually on the money with the stuff they share — but skewed sales and "breaking records" can still go hand-in-hand! It’s often around 60/40 — 60 for PlayStation and 40 for Xbox — which is much better than the console sales ratio. The difference is that the PlayStation community has far more casual gamers and generally lower engagement. In any case, that doesn’t contradict the fact that Xbox is breaking sales records. That’s where he’s wrong. That’s his livelihood — all of it just to sell subscriptions. Honestly, the whole controversy is ridiculous. It just shows that, in my view, Tom Warren isn’t reliable. The fact that he replies with “what’s the Xbox console market share?” basically reveals that he’s basing everything solely on that number. It’s a simplistic shortcut anyone with a shallow understanding could make. You don’t need sources to say something like that — and that’s exactly what he’s doing. He’s been wrong many times before (Game Pass ending, Starfield day one on PS5, Xbox consoles being discontinued, Xbox leaving the European market, etc.). The thing is, he wraps misinformation around true facts, which makes him look credible — but let’s be honest, it’s business. He sells sensationalism behind his paid subscriptions. He’s clearly both judge and jury, and that’s a conflict of interest. We’re basically in a world where a simple leaker thinks he has more authority and holds the truth over the actual source of truth.
